text:
Ana: morning handoff — quick summary for the north shift. overnight we saw a couple of high-severity pages tied to GPU node evictions in eu-west. impact: increased p95 inference latency and a small spike in streaming timeouts for calls routed to the dedicated pool. customer visible: intermittent 504s for long-stream responses (~2% of traffic to the dedicated pool).

Mike: noted. which model/route is most affected?

Ana: it’s concentrated on routes serving the commander-1 family (long-context streaming). traffic routing is partial — most requests fall back to hosted pool, but the dedicated nodes that had the eviction are still flapping.

PagerBot: INC-7843 created by auto-page at 2026-03-15T02:14:22Z — triggers: sustained kube eviction events >2m for nodes eu-west-1a. Severity: P1 -> Alerting secondary.

DevOps Bot: recent events from k8s: 
```
kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -l pool=dedicated-euw -o wide
# several pods in CrashLoopBackOff then Running
journalctl -u kubelet | grep eviction
# OOM kills with kernel lru reclaim warnings
```

Tasha: I started a node drain and re-provision on the affected ASG. scaling up the reserved capacity to +2 nodes now (in progress). ETA ~6-8m. Will update when terraform apply finishes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Simon: I can own on-call diag. first steps: confirm which pods evicted, check kernel OOMs, and validate node autoscaler activity. pinging @Elena if you can open a support ticket with infra for a closer look at host-level metrics (dmesg, memory spikes).

Elena: opening ticket INC-7843-SUPP now. adding node snapshots and dmesg output. Also grabbing cloudprovider logs for the ASG.

Mike: for mitigation — can we fail over traffic for long-stream routes to hosted pool automatically? if so, do it and monitor for request quality regressions. If not, we'll enable a temporary routing rule to prefer hosted variants for commander-1 streams.

Ana: routing fallback is configured as a policy but not flipped. steps I’m recommending now: 
1) force traffic shift for commander-1 streaming -> hosted pool (manual flip).
2) scale dedicated pool by +2 nodes (Tasha doing).
3) Simon to triage node OOMs and confirm kernel regressions.
4) Elena to attach infra ticket and collect core dumps.
5) Mike to watch p95 and 504 rate in the streaming dashboard, and wake me if >3% or p95 >1.2x baseline.

Quick command snippets: 
```
# force routing flip (internal console command)
redwoodctl routing set prefer-hosted --route commander-1/streaming --until 2026-03-15T06:00:00Z

# check pods
kubectl describe pod <pod> -n redwood-serving
journalctl -k | grep -i oom
```

PagerBot: Route policy change requested by Ana at 2026-03-15T03:02:14Z. Approval required from secondary on-call.

Tasha: approved. I’ll apply the flip and post back.

Simon: on it — pulling logs now. preliminary: two nodes reported heavy buffer cache pressure then OOM kill on container runtime. adding to INC-7843 notes. :mag:

Ana: thanks. current status when I post this: routing flip requested, dedicated pool scaling in progress, infra ticket open. Customer impact: low but rising if nodes keep flapping (2%-> could hit 5% on surge). Next steps: watch for ASG stabilization, confirm node health, and keep fallback route until 06:00 UTC. If the flip doesn't reduce 504s in 10m, escalate to infra lead.

Mike: will monitor dashboards and metrics. I’ll post p95/504 every 5m until stabilized.

Elena: support ticket updated with logs + node snapshot. asking infra for host memory histograms and dmesg analysis.

Tasha: terraform apply done. nodes provisioning -> waiting for k8s readiness. I’ll run a smoke test when pods are healthy.

Simon: smoke test plan: send 500 synthetic streamer requests over 1m and check for any 5xx. commands: 
```
python tools/stream_test.py --route commander-1 --concurrency 50 --duration 60
```

Ana: wrap-up notes for next shift: primary = Mike, secondary = Simon. if not resolved by handoff, escalate to infra lead and tag INC-7843 as ongoing. runbook: https://console.redwood/internal/runbooks/eviction-and-ooms (see sections 2.1 -> 2.4).

Mike: ack. will take primary. logging this handoff to the rota. :white_check_mark:
